html:
The Cochinchina campaign was the French and Spanish war against Vietnam from 1858 to 1862, which ended with France taking Saigon and the southern provinces, the start of French rule in Indochina.

France used the persecution of Catholic missionaries by the Nguyễn emperors as its reason. A fleet attacked Da Nang in 1858, then turned south and took Saigon in 1859. In the Treaty of Saigon of 1862 Emperor Tự Đức ceded three southern provinces, and France took the rest of the south in 1867.

France went on to take the north and centre in the 1880s and formed French Indochina in 1887, adding Cambodia and later Laos. Saigon became a French city of rubber and rice trade. Resistance never died, leading at last to the August Revolution and the First Indochina War.
